items.title: Over a catenary Noetherian local normal domain every radical ideal contains a nonzero element whose quotient is reduced
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The proposition takes a catenary Noetherian local normal domain R of dimension d and a radical ideal J, and asserts the existence of a nonzero f in J with R/fR reduced (source lines 38386-38396). The proof spells out in full what the shorter radical-element lemma does, and the catenary hypothesis is used essentially: it makes every height one prime have dimension d - 1, so that the spectrum of R/(f + h) is equidimensional and the height-one-polynomial lemma applies (proof lines 38405-38409). The proof then sets up the divisor div(f) = sum m_j q_j over the height one primes containing f, observes that R/fR is reduced exactly when all m_j equal 1, and uses that R/fR embeds into the product of its localizations at those primes (proof lines 38414-38434). It introduces t(y) as the number of minimal primes over y and, using the catenary property together with the height-one-polynomial lemma, bounds t(f + h) independently of h in the power m^N (proof lines 38437-38459). Maximality of t over h in m^N cap J is then used to replace f so that t(f + h) <= s for all such h (proof lines 38462-38467), after which the desired h is manufactured: elements a_j in q_j cap J avoiding the other q_j' and elements b_j in J cap q_1 cap ... cap q_s outside the second symbolic power q_j^{(2)}, combined into c = sum b_j prod a_j', then multiplied by the a_j with m_j = 1 and by a suitable y (proof lines 38470-38512). The non-routine content is the boundedness of t, which is what makes the maximality argument possible, and the prime-avoidance construction of c with prescribed valuations.
